# Dropwire

Dropwire is a free, open-source, peer-to-peer file transfer app for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It sends files directly device to device, end-to-end encrypted (QUIC/TLS 1.3), with no accounts and no servers holding your files. It works across the internet, not just on a local network.

## Quick facts
- Free forever: no trial, paywall, file-size limit, or ads
- Privacy-first: end-to-end encrypted; no accounts, no trackers, no analytics
- Peer-to-peer: files go directly device-to-device, and devices find each other over the public Mainline DHT. n0's free public relay (from the team behind iroh) is a fallback only: it forwards encrypted bytes and cannot read or store files. The project runs no servers of its own
- Works across the internet, not LAN-only
- Open source: dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0; audit, build, or fork it
- Current version: 0.3.0 (Tauri desktop app)

## How it works
1. Pick a file, several files, or a folder (drag them in or browse)
2. Share the one-time transfer code (the recipient pastes it into Receive), or tap a nearby device on the same network
3. Recipient previews names/sizes/count (verified by the code), accepts, and receives it, end-to-end encrypted

## Key features
- Nearby devices: apps on the same network discover each other over mDNS and appear as one-tap targets, so no code is needed locally. Both sides confirm before anything moves, and each shows a short pairing code to compare aloud. With nearby sharing off, the device stops advertising and refuses incoming requests
- One code, one recipient: the code works for the first device that connects; others are refused. It only works while the sender is sharing: once they cancel, dismiss the send, or quit, the code stops working, and they can resend from their history
- Preview before accept: see what's incoming before any byte downloads
- Direct vs relayed badge: live indicator of how the transfer is travelling
- Resumable transfers; multiple transfers at once; take only the files you want
- History stays on your device only, with a detail view per transfer: peer, code, route, timing, per-file breakdown, verified file list
- A desktop app, not a web page in a window: one fixed frame that draws its own title bar on all three platforms, nothing scrolls out of view, nothing needs resizing
- Tray: closing the window keeps Dropwire reachable; the tray icon reports state and its panel takes a dropped file or a pasted code, then opens the main window on it
- Trusted devices: a device is remembered after a transfer with it completes and can optionally skip the consent step; trust grants nothing on its own, since they still confirm on their side and you still see the file list before anything is saved
- Send text: send a snippet or the clipboard as a transfer, over the same encrypted path
- Notifications for three events only: a transfer finished, an offer arrived while you were away, and a failure that needs a decision. Progress never notifies

## How it compares
- vs WeTransfer: WeTransfer uploads files to its servers and limits file size; Dropwire sends peer-to-peer with no upload and no size limit, free
- vs Send Anywhere: Send Anywhere is closed-source with a paid tier; Dropwire is open source and free forever
- vs Snapdrop / AirDrop / LocalSend: those are LAN-only (AirDrop also Apple-only). Dropwire does the same nearby-device flow on a local network AND works across the internet with a code, so one app covers both
